bib.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for News Summarization

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Benchmarking Large Language Models for News Summarization", Tianyi Zhang*, Faisal Ladhak*, Esin Durmus, Percy Liang, Kathleen McKeown, Tatsunori B. Hashimoto. Preprint: the only venue mark printed is "arXiv:2301.13848v1 [cs.CL] 31 Jan 2023". Affiliations as printed (typos theirs): Zhang "Stanford Univeristy", Ladhak "Columbia Univeristy" (equal contribution).

COVERAGE: 14 of 14 pages, 55,326 of 55,326 chars. Body is p1-10, references p11-14 (skimmed). There is no appendix.

The note path you gave, `generative-ai/08-eval/notes/02-metrics-and-graders.md`, does not exist. `notes/` has `02-defining-correct.md` and `04-graders.md`, so I read without a note.

Two things you asked for are not in this version:
- **Summary-level correlations:** none are reported. Only system-level Kendall's tau (Table 3).
- **A correlation number with freelance references:** none is given. Section 4.3 and Figure 6 are scatter plots and prose only.

CLAIMS

1. Human evaluation design (p3-4)
- Ten LLMs plus fine-tuned Pegasus and BRIO plus the existing references; "18 model settings and two datasets" (p2).
- 100 articles from each of the CNN/DM and XSUM validation sets.
- Zero-shot covers only the six OpenAI models; all ten are run five-shot. Temperature 0.3.
- MTurk, three annotators per summary, scores averaged.
- quote (p4): "Coherence and relevance ratings are collected on a 1 to 5 Likert scale while faithfulness ratings are collected in binary ratings". Fluency is omitted.
- No inter-annotator agreement is reported for this MTurk study.

2. References rate below most systems (Table 2, p4)
- quote: "Existing references - 0.84 3 .20 3 .94 0 .37 4 .13 3 .00" (CNN/DM faithfulness, coherence, relevance, then XSUM).
- Zero-shot Instruct Davinci on the same axes: 0.99 / 4.15 / 4.60 and 0.97 / 4.41 / 4.28.
- Five-shot prompting with XSUM references hurts: "the faithfulness score of Instruct Davinci drops from 0.97 to 0.77" (p5).

3. Metric correlation tracks reference quality (Table 3, p6; system-level Kendall's tau, original references)

| Metric | CNN/DM faith. | CNN/DM coh. | CNN/DM rel. | XSUM faith. | XSUM coh. | XSUM rel. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rouge-L | 0.54 | 0.48 | 0.72 | -0.27 | 0.71 | 0.30 |
| METEOR | 0.58 | 0.37 | 0.66 | -0.22 | 0.68 | 0.38 |
| BertScore | 0.54 | 0.47 | 0.70 | -0.23 | 0.70 | 0.30 |
| BARTScore | 0.56 | 0.34 | 0.65 | -0.22 | 0.70 | 0.35 |
| BLEURT | 0.56 | 0.62 | 0.81 | -0.08 | 0.67 | 0.41 |

- quote (p6): "reference-based metrics correlate better with human judgments on the aspects for which reference summaries also have better scores (e.g. CNN/DM relevance, XSUM coherence)".
- Rouge-L still ranks fine-tuned models above LLMs on CNN/DM. Among LLMs only, "a larger than 0.05 Rouge-L difference usually translates to improved human evaluation" (p6).
- With freelance references on XSUM faithfulness, the result is qualitative: "which leads to a much more positive correlation" (p9).

4. Freelance writers (p6-9)
- Six Upwork writers, 50 articles per dataset, three writers per article, about 50 words, $4 per article.
- MTurk check on 100 summaries (Table 4, p7): "Freelance Writer 0.93 4.39 4.26", Instruct Davinci 0.98 / 4.26 / 4.40, references 0.64 / 3.59 / 3.45.
- Extractiveness (p8): "coverage and density for Instruct Davinci generated summaries are 0.92 and 12.1 whereas those for the writers written summaries are 0.81 and 2.07".
- Blinded pairwise comparison: six Upwork annotators, the same 100 pairs each. Overall preference is 50.4% writers against 49.6% Instruct Davinci (Figure 5).
- Agreement (p9): informativeness "Krippendorff's alpha is 0.32"; overall preference "Krippendorff's alpha is 0.07".
- Individual annotators range from 43.0% to 56.9% preferring the writers.

5. Instruction tuning, not size (p1, p4)
- quote (p1): "even a 350M parameter instruction-tuned GPT-3 can perform on par with the 175B parameter GPT-3."
- Zero-shot CNN/DM: GPT-3 175B scores 0.76 / 2.65 / 3.50; Ada Instruct 350M scores 0.88 / 4.02 / 4.26.

LIMITS
- News only, English, two datasets, 100 articles each; the paired comparison is 100 pairs and six raters.
- The cut-and-paste analysis covers ten summary pairs.
- Size and instruction tuning are compared only within OpenAI models, whose training details are "inferred by us based on the API naming scheme" (p3).
- The authors concede fine-tuned models may be underestimated because of poor training data.
- No LLM-as-judge and no reference-free metrics are tested.
- Dated: the models are 2022 vintage.

BUILDS ON
- Fabbri et al. (2020), SummEval: the annotation guidelines.
- Maynez et al. (2020): XSUM unfaithfulness.
- Freitag et al. (2020): reference quality in machine translation.
- Goyal et al. (2022): GPT-3 news summarization.
- Jing and McKeown (2000): cut-and-paste operations.
- Grusky et al. (2018): coverage and density.
- Liu et al. (2022a): length as a confound.

CODE: none. The prompt is on p3: "Article: [article]. Summarize the article in three sentences. Summary:".

FIGURES: Figure 6, p10, "System-level Rouge-L vs. annotating rating of faithfulness", XSUM references on the left and freelance references on the right. It shows the same metric flipping from a negative to a positive relationship when only the references change.

PROBLEMS
- The extraction is clean and contains no embedded instructions.
- Section 3.3 says "six popular automatic metrics" but lists and tabulates five.
- The p5 text cites "Table 3" where Table 2 is meant.
- Table 4 says its Instruct Davinci and reference rows are averaged from Table 2, but the simple means do not match (reference faithfulness would be 0.605, not 0.64). The basis for those rows is unclear, so quote them as printed.
- The informativeness figure is 51.1% in the text and 51.2% in Figure 5.
- The 350M GPT-3 five-shot XSUM row is blank because the model produced empty outputs.
